headline: Protesters besieged Pirgachha Police Station over JCD leader's death
summary: Over 200 people, including relatives of Chhatra Dal leader Monowarul Islam Bokshi, protested in Rangpur alleging police involvement in his death.
details: Relatives and local residents besieged Pirgachha Police Station in Rangpur on Saturday, protesting the death of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) leader Monowarul Islam Bokshi.
Monowarul, 29, the vice-president of the Savar unit of JCD, died after falling from the rooftop of a residential building during a police operation in Savar, Dhaka, early Friday.
The operation was conducted by officers from Pirgachha Police Station, assisted by Savar police, while searching for a missing teenage girl and her companion.
Protesters, who brought Monowarul's body to the police station premises, blocked the road in front of the station, demanding a fair investigation and punishment for those responsible.
The situation was brought under control after the intervention of local political leaders.
The family of the deceased has stated they are preparing to file a case with Savar Model Police Station to seek justice for Monowarul.
Pirgachha Police Station's officer-in-charge, Selim Malik, advised the relatives to file a case, stating that the actual circumstances will emerge through investigation.
caption:
Over 200 people besieged a police station in Rangpur, demanding justice for a Chhatra Dal leader who died during a police operation.

Relatives and local residents besieged Pirgachha Police Station in Rangpur on Saturday, protesting the death of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) leader Monowarul Islam Bokshi.

Monowarul, 29, the vice-president of the Savar unit of JCD, died after falling from the rooftop of a residential building during a police operation in Savar, Dhaka, early Friday.

The operation was conducted by officers from Pirgachha Police Station, assisted by Savar police, while searching for a missing teenage girl and her companion.

Protesters, who brought Monowarul's body to the police station premises, blocked the road in front of the station, demanding a fair investigation and punishment for those responsible.

The situation was brought under control after the intervention of local political leaders.

The family of the deceased has stated they are preparing to file a case with Savar Model Police Station to seek justice for Monowarul.

Pirgachha Police Station's officer-in-charge, Selim Malik, advised the relatives to file a case, stating that the actual circumstances will emerge through investigation.

headline_marked: Galle Gallants [[win maiden LPL title]] as Shakib and Hridoy's Jaffna Kings lose
headline: Galle Gallants win maiden LPL title as Shakib and Hridoy's Jaffna Kings lose
summary: The Gallants secured a five-wicket victory in the final on Saturday, ending the Jaffna Kings' bid for a fourth consecutive championship.
details: Galle Gallants claimed their first-ever Lanka Premier League title by defeating Jaffna Kings by five wickets in the final on Saturday.
Jaffna Kings, opting to bat first, were bowled out for 123 in 19.3 overs. Opener Kamil Mishara top-scored with 41, while Charith Asalanka and Eshan Malinga took three wickets each for the Gallants.
Bangladesh's Tawhid Hridoy scored only 10 off 10 balls, failing to repeat his record-fastest fifty from the qualifier.
Shakib Al Hasan produced a strong bowling spell, claiming two wickets for 15 runs, but his efforts were not enough to keep the Gallants from reaching the target.
The Gallants' chase was led by Thomas Fraser Rogers (34 off 27) and Dinura Kalupahana (31 off 19), who shared a 64-run partnership.
Despite a brief collapse triggered by Shakib taking two wickets in a single over, the Gallants reached 123 in 15.5 overs, winning with 25 balls to spare.
caption:
Galle Gallants claim their first LPL title! 🏆

Shakib Al Hasan and Tawhid Hridoy's Jaffna Kings fall short in the final.

Galle Gallants claimed their first-ever Lanka Premier League title by defeating Jaffna Kings by five wickets in the final on Saturday.

Jaffna Kings, opting to bat first, were bowled out for 123 in 19.3 overs. Opener Kamil Mishara top-scored with 41, while Charith Asalanka and Eshan Malinga took three wickets each for the Gallants.

Bangladesh's Tawhid Hridoy scored only 10 off 10 balls, failing to repeat his record-fastest fifty from the qualifier.

Shakib Al Hasan produced a strong bowling spell, claiming two wickets for 15 runs, but his efforts were not enough to keep the Gallants from reaching the target.

The Gallants' chase was led by Thomas Fraser Rogers (34 off 27) and Dinura Kalupahana (31 off 19), who shared a 64-run partnership.

Despite a brief collapse triggered by Shakib taking two wickets in a single over, the Gallants reached 123 in 15.5 overs, winning with 25 balls to spare.
